intro: A three-minute checkpoint on the first half of this module, in your own AI assistant with voice on: guessing and reporting. The tutor describes evidence and asks what you conclude (Was vermuten Sie? — muss / dürfte / könnte + infinitive, present or past), then gives you rumours and self-claims to relay (soll / will). It listens for the modal matching the stated certainty, for the Infinitiv II when the guess is about the past, for the distinction between soll and will. Speak in full sentences; say 'Ende' if you need to stop early.
tips[0].title: Evidence → modal + infinitive
tips[0].text: Nasse Straße → Es muss geregnet haben. Kein Auto → Er könnte verreist sein. Volle Mailbox → Er dürfte länger weg sein. Match the modal to how sure the evidence makes you.
tips[0].check.why: For your own near-certain conclusion use muss + Infinitiv II; soll reports what others say and will reports a self-claim.
tips[1].title: Rumour → soll; self-claim → will
tips[1].text: 'Man sagt, sie hat gewonnen' → Sie soll gewonnen haben. 'Er sagt, er war nicht dort' → Er will nicht dort gewesen sein.
tips[1].check.why: When someone claims something about himself, use will + Infinitiv II; soll would mean other people say it.
tips[1].visual.rows[0].b: Er will es nicht gewusst haben.
remember[0]: muss / dürfte / könnte + (Partizip II + haben/sein) for guesses.
remember[1]: soll = they say; will = he says.
hook: Turn clues and rumours into confident German: show how sure you are with dürfte or muss, and pass on claims with soll and will.
